interpretation.total: Current v15 one-shot spec locally -1.9888% CI[-3.5561,-0.3960] in this eight-block report. Earlier four-block v15 -1.6253% CI[-6.1572,+3.1254] and the user-reported controlled comparison did not establish a stable cross-environment gain. No admission claim.
interpretation.physicalIndex: Restoring a full index on the same direct-AST path costs +8.1470% CI[+4.6201,+11.7929]. This includes the indexed-row adapter; not a transferable isolated 8.1470% optimization of the original parser.
interpretation.locator: Reusing the already-built index for inline locations instead of a second streaming locator: -2.3313% CI[-7.2464,+2.8442], unresolved. Source mapping sampling changes are not an independent established gain.
interpretation.residual: With full index and original locator, the new block pipeline is +2.0457% CI[+1.3412,+2.7551] against production. Includes adapter, container views, AST/jobs and SourceView changes; does not isolate direct AST alone. Removing BlockTokenStream is not established as an independent net gain.
interpretation.nonAdditivity: Ratios from independent pairs are not additive contributions. JIT/GC, adapter overhead and physical-index/locator interactions prevent an exact per-component percentage decomposition.
interpretation.userProfile: The four user-reported categories sum to 613.2ms baseline and 419.5ms current (-193.7ms); without raw total and mutually exclusive complete classification this is not a causal attribution of net parser latency.
interpretation.nextBoundary: Retain BlockScanner, BlockTokenStream and exact incremental correspondence. Pursue independently attributable redundant work inside the existing model. Do not re-run historical line-layout, RegExp line-stream, same-line locator or zero-state-write candidates without a changed invariant.

2026-11-15，Apple M1 Pro，Node v24.22.1 / v26.13.0。基线为本轮开始时的用户工作区，包含既有未暂存 Latin1 更改；不是与 HEAD 或暂存版比较。

## 保留的结构

生产改动仅在 `packages/satorigear/src/block/lines.ts`，保持未暂存。构造、重建入口从 constructor / from / scan / #scan 收敛为 constructor / scan。

- 构造函数只初始化容器，并补齐已有无参调用所需的零值默认参数。基线的 `capacity` 未传时产生零长度数组；默认容量仍为零。
- 实例 `scan` 管理源长度、定位游标、容量和最终状态；只在这里发布 fields / count / normalized。
- `Latin1.scan` 与文件内 `scanLineFields` 使用相同的输入输出约定：输入字符串和行数组，返回 count / fields / normalized。普通内核不再接收 BlockLines 实例或访问其私有字段。
- 删除只有一个调用点的 `from`。增量 `update` 自己隔离重建片段并平移坐标；切片仍防止末尾 CR 消耗片段以外的 LF。临时行表的 sourceLength 是片段长度；它只参与几何复制和 normalized 合并，不对外充当定位器。
- `lineCapacity` 统一扫描与局部重建使用的容量估算；保留预分配策略，避免局部重建从零容量反复增长。

Latin1 类源码逐字保持一致，扫描阈值、缓冲复用和输入分流规则未增加特例。实例状态管理集中到一个入口，两个内核具有一致的数据约定。

earlierSameGoal.note: Short slices are faster per character. A full-source search overscans and is slower.

boundary-marker-kernel-6485d8c-node26-m1.attribution: On the current spec profile the boundary RegExp is about 8.5% of the parse and nextBoundaryOffset about 2.4%. The marker-only class is faster on these slices (0.126 vs 0.1495) because it does not stop for newlines. That is about 0.02 ms, roughly 2% of a 0.96 ms spec parse, before any correctness repair. Putting newline classification back with indexOf, per-line slices, or a second scan of the same text costs more than that gap. Per-line slices were already slower with the slice cost excluded.

Do not replace paragraph slices with a full-source or per-line boundary search. Resume only when the existing line walk already classifies those endings, the tokenizer still has one explicit input, and a fresh ABBA shows a spec speedup. code-leaf-line-hint-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.status: Measured, reverted. Not a remark ratio. The paragraph-continuation fast path stays.
code-leaf-line-hint-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.question: Does a line argument on the shared locationAt let a code leaf skip the forward walk across its body?
code-leaf-line-hint-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.attribution: On the paragraph-continue spec profile the code builder's locationAt is 35/2150 samples and the samples sit on the forward compare (21 ticks), not on the return. One spec parse has 708 code blocks whose interiors are not re-queried once the cursor sits on the end line. The candidate stored those line indexes and taught the shared locationAt an optional line. That code-builder node fell to 11/2137 samples, and its ticks are the hint return, so the interior walk did disappear. Every other position still calls the same function. Total locationAt rose from 89/2150 (4.14%) to 124/2137 (5.80%). The paragraph literal walk rose from 13 samples to 26. placedLine, the new metadata read, is 9 samples. Isolated 8-block ABBA versus the paragraph-continue bundle is slower where positions dominate: spec +0.83% [+0.25, +1.41], examples +1.12% [+0.31, +1.93], apis +2.65% [+1.55, +3.77], all entirely above zero. Rust and tail cross zero. The line check on the shared function costs more than the code-leaf walk it removes.
code-leaf-line-hint-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.repeatGate: Do not add an optional line parameter to locationAt or positionAt, and do not reformat that shared function to make room for the check. Resume only with a separate method whose source leaves locationAt unchanged, and only while a profile still shows the code-builder walk as a long compare rather than a one-line return.

comparisons.kernel-attribution.json: Uniform current-row consumer with original dense kernel -> same consumer with local scan counter and locator cursor. No grammar/protocol change.

protocol.method: Alternating ABBA/BAAB; fresh process and module cache per observation; GC before warmup and settling; natural GC included; all samples retained.

interpretation: Local counter/cursor writes have no supported speedup. They do not explain the prior regression.
Dense local-kernel current-row parser regresses spec and examples. Four-field-backed current-row parser also regresses spec.

Restoring four-field geometry does not show a benefit versus the dense variant (CI crosses zero). This is not proof of equivalence and does not prove that removing dense/packed line facts is intrinsically slow.
The production-vs-packed contrast includes all new grammar-consumer/control costs; it must not be presented as a precise causal measurement of the row protocol alone.
Counter diagnostics show identical ordered inline input text hashes and equal inline boundary/token/location counts. Short sampled CPU profiles are not evidence of extra inline work.

Current-row consumer avoids 663 projected-row writes and 17 lazy-tail probes on spec but performs 9760 physical prepare calls and 10421 row-consume calls; only 2 cursor forks occur. Counts do not prove a time breakdown.

Stop tuning this all-current-row implementation. Next architecture should preserve range advancement rather than requiring a materialized mutable current physical row at every consumed line. Do not rerun prior storage layouts, getter variants, sparse checkpoints or raw-fence regex routes without a new relevant invariant.

Production performance target not achieved.
currentModel: Grammar handlers construct final block AST nodes directly. No complete physical/projected line table, block token arena, node-length/role traversal, or semantic-anchor array is built by the new parse path.

Only inline region source facts wait for the complete definition set: source range pairs where prefixes create gaps, first physical line start/ordinal/end, and an AST owner. Existing generated inline tokenization/resolution/projection is reused.

RangeView consumes source spans directly; removed the fake BlockTokenStream adapter and synthetic tokenStart/nodeLength protocol from source projection. Inline projection still borrows the old buildInlineFragment cursor interface; removing that remaining adapter is a next action.

Parser-owned inline workspaces are reused. AST/range references are cleared after projection; prior returned ASTs remain independent across subsequent parses. No parse result or source-identity memoization.

Block positions are produced while the relevant row is current. Indented-code end facts are captured at the last content row, independently of consumed trailing blank rows. Removed root previous-end/previous-ordinal state; retained previous-start for bounded forward blank checking.

Definitions borrow the current row until a still-rejectable cross-row read is needed. A valid prefix is committed before optional next-line title probing, so ordinary single-line definitions do not copy a destination cursor or adopt copies of unchanged state.

The latest reader keeps physical current-row geometry ready. Root loaded cache flag removed; quote/list current-prefix caches remain grammar-owned. Codegen is preserved, with the same grammar probes used in CSP fallback.

No new feature flags, production API, token metadata, special list close protocol or parser-detail tests were added. These facts do not prove that a complete feature/edit migration will be simpler or faster.

measurementInterpretation: Flat cache +49.77% spec: rejected. Direct AST initially +4.58% spec/+24.18% examples; progressively aligned workspace ownership and removed old-model adapters.
Definition-sensitive eager scheduling increased spec time; it was removed rather than retaining extra dependency epochs/view ownership without a demonstrated benefit.

An intermediate candidate established -1.56% spec with eight blocks but +4.54% examples and +11.15% default Rust: not promotable. The source snapshots and intervals remain tied to their original hashes.
Removing placeholder children arrays had no measurable isolated examples benefit: +0.19%, CI crosses zero. It is only a representation simplification, not credited performance.

Lazy reference transactions alone improve default Rust versus the preceding prototype by -7.3858335474%, CI [-11.2561939708,-3.3466761063]. This is recovery of prototype overhead, not a new production gain.

Latest measured snapshot vs production: spec -0.9678%, examples -0.7719%, default Rust +0.9009%, default APIs +3.9443%; every 95% interval crosses zero. Neither cumulative gain nor strict non-inferiority is established.
Rust/APIs guards disable extensions on both sides. They are not the repository stock feature-enabled cases, and cannot be compared numerically to those historical measurements.

After measurement, restored the CRLF interior-offset guard in the per-region locator. Corrected bundle revalidated against public parse output, but not rebenchmarked. No timing is transferred to that corrected source.

runtimeEvidence.gc: No large amplification established in A/B spec profile. Allocation itself is not isolated as the causal regression.
runtimeEvidence.comparisonAttribution: Keeping the string descriptor and restoring original comparison/control flow improves B by 2.97% CI[-4.39,-1.53]. Cannot attribute this entire delta to string representation or to one native instruction.
runtimeEvidence.branchAttribution: N performs 1157 marker-length-check attempts in the recorded insertion where A performs none. Both receive 2324 close calls due to actual incremental rescan behavior. Shorter code removed an early negative proof.
runtimeEvidence.phaseProbeLimits: Whole-phase timers add instrumentation and include natural GC. One-in-sixteen inline-region estimates use rotating selection and include wrapper/clock overhead, finite-sample imbalance and possible GC correlation. They guide architecture work, not throughput admission or exact causal percentages.

validation.BAndR: Public AST/position and fence/projected-body matrices passed; only N received the full final source/CSP/edit guard set. Not a claim of full admission for B/R.
validation.countsProvenance: Stored JSON reports plus successful validator terminal output; matrix scripts assert expected counts.

disposition.repeatGate: Do not repeat per-fence string descriptors/startsWith, re-derived numeric marker, or removal of the indentation early rejection without a new lifetime/consumer invariant. disposition.nextFocus: Whole-phase evidence places material cost in physical indexing and inline tokenize/resolve/projection. Require a change eliminating complete passes/events or ownership duplication, checked against prior experiments, rather than further fence/layout micro-tuning.

fence-info-split-a73acfe-node26-m1pro.js.status: Measured, reverted. Not a remark ratio. The absolute line coordinates and the whitespace-break boolean stay.
fence-info-split-a73acfe-node26-m1pro.js.question: Does recording the backtick info split during the forbidden-marker scan remove the code builder's semanticText and first space search?
fence-info-split-a73acfe-node26-m1pro.js.attribution: On the kept spec profile, semanticText is 32/3099 hits (1.03%) and the code builder's first /[ \t]/ search is 25 ticks (0.81%). Spec fence info is almost all plain: one opening line contains \\ or &. The candidate kept that classification on the backtick scan, which already walks the info line to reject a nested marker, and the builder skipped semanticText when the index was present. The meta-word search stayed, because an entity can still change the tail. semanticText fell to 5/2082 hits (0.24%). The replacement walk is plainBacktickInfo at 12 hits (0.58%) plus trimLineWhitespaceStart at 37 hits (1.78%), up from 30/3099 (0.97%). fenceAt stayed 3.41%, and 61 of its 71 ticks are still the marker-run loop. The trim call and the extra \\ / & / space tests cost as much as the builder calls they removed. Isolated 8-block ABBA versus the kept absolute bundle does not establish a spec speedup: −0.52% [−1.36, +0.33]. Examples are +0.90% [−0.35, +2.16]. No case lands entirely below zero. Kept remark estimate remains 85.05×.

fence-range-research-fed4f91-node26-m1pr.status: Fully withdrawn after independently confirmed fence-window incremental regression. No production source or test change retained; no new source commit or fixed-remark ratio update.
fence-range-research-fed4f91-node26-m1pr.intent: Consume opaque fenced ranges through one shared operation; replace component cross-row codeFence state with an immediate range skip. Preserve full physical index, token model, metadata, grammar and AST ownership.

nativeSearchUnmeasured.status: Stopped without timing after discovering prior equivalent exact/native fence searches in older cache. No new invariant justified retry. Default AST/edit/source validation had passed before duplicate discovery.
nativeSearchUnmeasured.note: Would retain original close predicate and source-search opening run, unlike sparse-index route, but the older standalone exact/native search already covered this cost shape. Do not repeat under a different helper name.

helper.status: Validated and measured, not retained separately. Net -2 production lines. No isolated throughput improvement established.
helper.model: Make closesFence private; export fenceEnd that loops over original close predicate. Code, math, component close and component slot search share range consumption. No new feature registration/API, token fields, persistent cache or semantic model.
helper.limits: This version did not resolve any throughput benefit, and the final unified-range candidate failed non-regression; no claim that the helper-only version itself has a proven regression.

inlined.status: Rejected on whole-candidate non-regression. Net -6 production lines; closesFence removed and its logic inlined in fenceEnd.
inlined.semanticChange: No intended grammar or output change. A per-line rejection becomes continue; an accepted close returns its line; no close returns the exclusive range limit.
inlined.causalLimit: Helper -> inlined alone +0.3784% CI[-1.4656,+2.2569], not an established difference. Therefore whole-candidate regression cannot be assigned to manual inlining. No V8 inlining/optimization mechanism was measured or claimed.

validation.testingScope: Existing source and CSP tests plus public syntax AST/positions and public edit feature E2E comparisons. No new parser-private tests. Fence/body matrix counts were observed in terminal output; scripts and validation summary retained.

generated-boundary-step-a73acfe-node26-m.status: Measured, reverted. Not a remark ratio. The absolute line coordinates and the whitespace-break boolean stay.
generated-boundary-step-a73acfe-node26-m.question: Is the nextBoundaryOffset frame a call that the generated tokenizer can remove by inlining those four steps?
generated-boundary-step-a73acfe-node26-m.attribution: The generated tokenizer calls nextBoundaryOffset through a new Function parameter, so V8 leaves that helper as its own frame (2.68% on the kept spec profile). Pasting the same length check, LF check, lastIndex store, and test into the generated loop removes the frame. The samples move into the generated function: anon rises from 3.03% to 5.80%, and 3.03+2.68=5.71. The boundary class stays 6.71% versus 6.74%. The call was not work above those four steps. Rust's interval versus the kept absolute bundle is entirely above zero. Spec's interval includes zero and the point estimate is slower. Kept remark estimate remains 85.05×.
generated-boundary-step-a73acfe-node26-m.repeatGate: Do not inline nextBoundaryOffset into the generated tokenizer. The parameter call is not extra work: its samples move into the generated function and the combined share stays about 5.7%. Rust was slower than the absolute-offset bundle. Do not retry a same-regex exec or matchAll spelling of this loop.

hard-break-event-c204d0b-node26-m1pro.js.status: Kept as representation simplification. No statistically established throughput gain or universal non-regression claim; no cumulative remark multiplier update.
hard-break-event-c204d0b-node26-m1pro.js.title: refactor: consume hard breaks as single inline events
hard-break-event-c204d0b-node26-m1pro.js.intent: Replace HardBreak+Newline cooperation with a complete hard-break event. Eliminate projection-time repair of an already emitted AST sibling.
representation: HardBreak End consumes the ending plus stripped continuation spaces; Data denotes the boundary after the physical ending and before continuation indentation.
The backslash feature recognizes and consumes its complete event; the existing newline lexer emits complete space-hard-break events in codegen and CSP.
The break builder owns its position end, using SourceView.mapEnd at the retained boundary. It does not ask a following token to repair a previous node.
Newline is exclusively a soft break and no longer carries an unused next-line-start fact. It uses Data=0.
No token fields, feature API, cross-parse cache, scanner line protocol, block model, AST ownership or incremental correspondence added.
hard-break-event-c204d0b-node26-m1pro.js.retentionReason: Removes cross-event sibling repair and 7 redundant spec tokens / 800 stress tokens. All interval estimates include zero; the API concern was followed by an independent eight-block confirmation near zero. Retained for clearer event ownership and fewer intermediate records, not a speed threshold or an established spec benefit. Total production net +3 lines, with newline-consumption logic now also explicit in backslash recognition.

inline-boundary-unification-a126216-node.status: E admitted and committed. B/C/D are not retained. Four incoming pending parser source edits remain unchanged and unadmitted.
inline-boundary-unification-a126216-node.sourceTitle: perf: unify inline boundary searches across profiles
inline-boundary-unification-a126216-node.intent: Remove the marker-count-dependent hard-space search prefix, using one boundary-discovery contract for every profile. Keep original LF-context matching, scanner codegen/CSP, token output, source mapping and incremental ownership.

variants.A: Accepted parser; >9 marker profile includes redundant leading-space hard-break alternative. Original LF then two-character lookbehind retained.
variants.B: Consume whitespace before LF instead of looking behind. No new state or protocol. Spec +14.7442%; closed after CPU/JIT investigation.
variants.C: Check preceding whitespace before consuming LF; retain the marker-count hard-space prefix. Spec confirmation -1.4020%; Rust +2.2101% confirmation. Not admitted.
variants.D: C plus removal of the hard-space prefix. Rust -3.4630%, but spec +2.4795% in its four-block batch. Not admitted.
variants.E: Only remove the marker-count hard-space prefix from A. Original LF pattern retained. Simpler uniform search selected after its own confirmation and guards.

inline-boundary-unification-a126216-node.protocol: Node 26.13.0 / M1 Pro; every build/test/performance command prefixed taskpolicy -c utility; alternating ABBA/BAAB; fresh process/module each observation; 250ms warmup, full GC, 150ms settling, approximately 300ms measured loop, every measured window <=500ms; natural GC and all observations retained; no own builds/tests/profiles concurrent with throughput. No M3 replication or new remark run.

attribution: B/C preserve 2384 boundary-discovery calls, 1570 raw inline tokens and 103298 view UTF-16 units in spec. Their changes move matching work, not token volume.

Spec inline views contain 1227 LF and 15286 horizontal whitespace units. B adds whitespace as a possible start. Its boundary self samples rise from 84.766 to 290.464 us/parse while native code is smaller. This supports expanded search work, not an exact native-comparison count.

C retains an extra full-feature hard-space alternative. With equal-length no-LF ordinary text, C is -2.4197% under the default profile but +3.1967% with full features and spaces; letter-only controls cross zero. This supports a profile/space interaction. It does not isolate one native instruction.

E removes that prefix rather than adding another profile branch. In the independent A/E Rust profiles, nextBoundaryOffset self samples are 1120.380 vs 897.379 us/parse; measured GC per parse is 1390.359 vs 1353.630 us. Sample attribution is not additive throughput accounting.

Separate uncluttered native-regexp logs show full-profile matcher sizes 1720/1880 B -> 1448/1600 B. The removed root alternative no longer admits spaces as initial matching positions. Production bundle decreases 51 B without minification.

E default CommonMark regex text is identical to A. The pooled spec elapsed change -1.37455% CI[-2.38127,-0.35745] must not be attributed to fewer boundary comparisons in that configuration. Batch variation, JIT/module-layout effects remain possible; no causal spec algorithm speedup is claimed.

E Rust first four blocks are -6.3881%, subsequent eight blocks -1.2117% with crossing-zero CI; all twelve blocks yield -2.96821%, CI[-4.88207,-1.01584]. Report all batches, not the favorable first estimate.

E guards: examples +0.2961% CI[-1.9014,+2.5427]; APIs -5.7412% CI[-8.0332,-3.3920]; tail edit -0.7667% CI[-2.7870,+1.2957]; document/spec -0.4718% CI[-2.3896,+1.4837]. Crossing zero is not proof of equivalence. No resolved guard regression was observed.

Long hard-break spaces improve -13.3494%, CI[-14.9409,-11.7283]; dense hard-break lines -1.4362%, CI[-2.8255,-0.0271]. These test the input class the removed prefix targeted, using public parse results.

D and C generate the same regex in the default configuration but showed differing spec timing. Native code size or source-level simplification alone cannot explain those batch differences; do not transfer C spec gain to D/E.

validation.eachVariantEachBackend: B/C/D/E each passed 2614 full corpus AST/position comparisons, 4608 feature edits, 5616 whitespace-boundary documents and 660 edits. Generated and forced-CSP paths both checked. E source and working combination also pass all 194 existing tests.
validation.sourceBuilds: All bundles use the standard production CLI; A hash equals the accepted historical frozen bundle. The final working bundle includes the four preserved pending edits and is not a throughput-admitted combination.
validation.plainRunnerSetupFailure: Initial cached TypeScript runner failed before any worker because Node cannot strip TypeScript under node_modules. Exact TS source was converted with stripTypeScriptTypes to .mjs and both retained; no performance observations dropped.

screenedIdea.disposition: Not implemented or benchmarked. Spec has zero escape/entity tokens in actual inline regions, so fusion cannot help this corpus. A sparse-escape workload could newly send 56519 source units through decoding; this is a cost risk, not a measured regression or general rejection.

inline-chunk-ownership-ea500ef-node26-m1.status: Kept as a model simplification; isolated comparisons do not establish a throughput gain or universal non-regression.
inline-chunk-ownership-ea500ef-node26-m1.title: refactor: discover inline regions from owned chunks
model: Inline content is defined by directly owned InlineChunk records, rather than a duplicated InlineContent kind bit.
Only frames with nodeLength >= 2 and an immediate InlineChunk child are inline owners; non-inline containers continue traversal.
Empty inline frames need no region. No new API, metadata, field, persistent ownership, close protocol, or feature discrimination.
ATX and later inline owner kinds follow the earlier open-frame kinds consecutively. A consumer-only variant retained old numeric kinds to isolate the membership change.

inline-line-cursor-a73acfe-node26-m1pro..attribution: locationAt fell from 5.5% to 2.2%, but locate took 1.8% and the publishers got heavier (appendRange 1.8%, createLiteralChildren 1.0%). splitHelper.question: Does splitting the line step out of the same-line allocator let V8 inline the publisher and beat the monotonic walk?
splitHelper.attribution: place was small enough to leave the top frames, and locationAt fell from 4.78% to 2.47%, but place, stepLine, and the per-view anchor put that time back. inline-projection-research-89ce055-node2.previousGoalTurnClassification: progress: recorded source allocation mappings, rejected extra semantic-plan representations, and produced a simpler boundary prototype with spec benefit but failing list guard. This turn changed the next action through exact work counts and real projection reuse.
modelProgress: Root bindings now own a reusable semantic inline fragment (children and pre-block-promotion attributes) alongside their AST target. Persistent syntax caches still contain only source/view/raw/resolved tokens, definition dependencies and geometry, with no AST references.

Reuse requires the same consumer and table-cell context, source spans outside the edit damage, identical first-row geometry, and identical mappings at both ends of every new contiguous source segment. Ordered gap-only mappings make these endpoint checks exact. No new SourceView or feature API.

Definition changes invalidate resolved tokens; render is the single place that resolves pending syntax and clears the corresponding semantic projection. Retained roots no longer resolve and separately invalidate output in another branch.

Cached pre-promotion attributes restore paragraph semantics when list looseness or quote structure changes; block postprocessors can move attributes again. Reusing only the final old paragraph would lose moved attributes.

ListCursor already stores a recognized sibling marker. That marker proves its own view has ended; subsequent peek returns false without recognizing the same boundary again. No new cache field, position-equality policy, close protocol or cursor reset lifecycle.

One-shot declaration stores membership only in the existing Map; document declaration increments counts with one lookup, retaining duplicate-definition removal semantics. The separate Set-class variant had no benefit and was withdrawn.

Removed research-only row/search/scope/reference counters, diagnostic getter, unused per-job range counting, and the reference try/finally used only to maintain counters. ObservedCursor already owns actual dependency probes. This removes prototype observation overhead, not a separately claimable production algorithm optimization.

findings: Local strings provide syntax bounds, not only offset translation. Unbounded original-source scanners cross real heading/paragraph/table-cell boundaries.

Original-source boundary search without cross-region reuse repeats suffix traversal: 800 plain paragraphs expand logical search spans from 8800 to 4165200 code units. This is a span count, not native character comparisons or a timing result.

A hypothetical ordered shared boundary result preserves bounded search answers in tested contiguous views; spec native calls 1894 -> 1670, API 10906 -> 4828. It does not remove bounded strings or segmented input, and scans farther overall.
SourceView shifts update current document coordinates independently of retained text. Original-source search state cannot safely follow mapped coordinates without current-source ownership.

js-parallel-line-scan-ab933fb-node26-m1p.status: Two pure-JS SWAR candidates rejected after runtime-guided adjustment. No production change.
js-parallel-line-scan-ab933fb-node26-m1p.report:
# Pure-JS parallel physical line scan

No production change retained or source commit created. Current baseline is ab933fb (upstream 096f1dc), Node 26.13.0 / Apple M1 Pro. This research does not establish an updated remark ratio or a universal impossibility result for JS parallel algorithms.

## Requirement and model

One scan algorithm handles LF, CR, CRLF, arbitrary UTF-16, partial scan ranges and edits. No corpus detection, length threshold, LF-only dispatch, alternate parser, feature API, WASM, worker thread, encoding, input copy, extra line representation or minification change.

The prototypes replace only the physical #scan body in frozen built bundles. The existing packed Start/End/Next/State table, growth policy, projection, locator and incremental consumers stay intact. These are executable research bundles, not admitted TypeScript source changes.

B packs two individually loaded UTF-16 code units into a 32-bit number. XOR with repeated CR/LF, subtract-and-mask zero-lane detection, then select the first actual ending. Cross-lane subtraction can contaminate individual lane bits, so the mask is used only as an any-match predicate; actual characters select the ending. CRLF consumption remains sequential at the event boundary.

C follows native-code inspection: first screen the common U+0008..U+000F control range with one zero-lane predicate, then refine actual CR/LF. It also retains the ending character already read, avoiding a redundant read. It treats tabs and other control characters normally; no source-class shortcut is selected. This is SWAR (parallel lanes within an integer), not a hardware SIMD API.

## Results

Positive means slower than A. Four alternating ABBA/BAAB blocks for each row, fresh process/module per observation, taskpolicy -c utility, 250 ms warmup, full GC, 150 ms settling, ~300 ms measurement and 500 ms cap; natural GC included. Own builds, tests, profiles and analysis do not overlap normal throughput. 64 normal observations; longest 299.086 ms. No M3 replication.

| Candidate | spec | 95% CI | examples | 95% CI |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| B, dual CR/LF lane predicates | +16.79% | [+15.22%, +18.38%] | +1.15% | [−1.08%, +3.42%] |
| C, shared coarse predicate and reused ending | +16.36% | [+14.84%, +17.89%] | +0.95% | [+0.05%, +1.85%] |

These are independent A/B and A/C comparisons; do not subtract them to claim a measured B/C improvement. Cross-zero intervals are not equivalence. Both fail the primary gate, so no further Rust/API/incremental/CSP throughput admission run was made.

## Actual runtime

Native logs distinguish warmup/OSR bodies from the last printed optimized body. Final #scan code: A 820 B, B 4544 B, C 2936 B. B/C contain scalar ldrb/ldrh string reads and bit operations, with no vector-register operations in these emitted scan bodies. Static scalar-load sites are 20/12 respectively; these include alternative string representations and duplicated loop code and are NOT runtime load counts. A delegates searches to native calls; its absence of vector instructions in the JS caller does not imply a scalar native search implementation.

Eight independent CPU profiles use ACCA/CAAC order, ~300 ms windows, monotonic timestamp clipping and at least 99.73% measured-interval coverage:

| Diagnostic, us/parse | A | C |
|---|---:|---:|
| #scan self samples (includes attributed native callees) | 242.02 | 365.81 |
| observed GC | 19.16 | 19.50 |
| profiled elapsed | 882.39 | 1025.43 |

Sampling and inlining shift attribution elsewhere; these figures are diagnostic, not an exact additive explanation. Native logs contain warmup deoptimizations; no phase-tagged JIT admission run was made, and no JIT-quiescence or measured-phase-zero-deopt claim is made. The evidence supports extra per-character string access/classification work, rather than a new temporary allocation or GC spike, as the principal investigated cost. Reducing predicate/native code size alone did not recover throughput.

## Public behavior verification

Both B and C, separately under generated and forced CSP, each pass 2986 complete AST/position comparisons and 560 edit operations checked against fresh parsing and baseline. Sources include standard corpora/default and full feature profiles, every UTF-16 code unit grouped across odd/even alignments, LF/CR/CRLF, mixed endings, containers, surrogate pairs and lone surrogates. No parser-private repository tests added. Baseline repository unit suite was not redundantly rerun for bundle-only prototypes. Candidate source build/typecheck is not claimed.

## Related research and limits

- simdjson obtains data parallelism from vector input classification and bit-mask/index extraction. Porting its bit arithmetic without its wide input loads is not equivalent: https://arxiv.org/html/1902.08318v7
- SIMD.js was archived; WebAssembly SIMD is a different execution interface, not a JS string vector-load operation: https://v8.dev/features/simd and https://github.com/tc39/ecmascript_simd
- Current upstream V8 single-character string search routes through FindFirstCharacter and memchr (this is source-level context, not proof of the exact local libc instruction sequence): https://github.com/v8/v8/blob/main/src/strings/string-search.h
- Workers provide actual thread parallelism and official Node docs recommend pools. A pool would still require source transfer/shared input, output ordering, boundary reconciliation and integration with the synchronous cross-platform parse interface. No worker throughput claim or prototype was made: https://nodejs.org/api/worker_threads.html

Historical scalar char loops, regex test/sticky streams, split/callback production, fixed-offset field writes, capacity loops and WASM encoding/copy kernels were reviewed, not rerun. The new two-lane classification is distinct from the prior scalar loop; its failure does not erase prior evidence. Do not reopen these B/C shapes by changing lane constants or unrolling without a demonstrated change to the input-loading or per-character-work premise.

Next architectural investigation must eliminate work beyond the bit predicate while preserving one generic source/line ownership model. This report does not nominate a previously rejected alternate line model as newly viable, and it does not propose benchmark-based fallback thresholds.

Copied/fused semantic plans, borrowed leaf slots and resolve-before-project scheduling did not solve the guard. No production source change or new accepted goal ratio.

modelChanges.boundary: Removed pending boundary objects and cross-loop match ownership. Removed a second generated interrupt dispatch and duplicate negative paragraph checks. Existing feature-owned pure interrupt predicates decide interruption once; actual block start recognizes its syntax when the next iteration starts. Keeps component interruption distinct from successful admission, including unclosed components. No new feature API or close protocol. Net raw research source -4 lines; primary simplification is the control model, not line count.
modelChanges.fusedSpan: Inline span itself replaces the extra job; semantic data is reused as the final AST payload, not spread/copied. Removed plan-to-AST map and persistent plan tree; publication traverses semantic spans and clears temporary plans. Still regresses spec +10.62% and list edits +43.68%; withdrawn.
modelChanges.leafSlots: Ordinary container ASTs remain direct. Only inline leaves borrow existing reusable job slots until complete projection; finalization replaces every slot before public return. No complete semantic plan graph or AST map/copy. Doc retains slots until fresh root materialization rather than overwriting them per group. Public retained-tree checks pass. Spec +0.42% with interval crossing zero, list +31.13% CI[+17.84,+45.92]; withdrawn.
modelChanges.phases: Only document scheduling changes: resolve all existing inline caches before materializing fresh ASTs, then project without lazy resolving inside render. No additional cache, metadata or intermediate representation. List +29.76% with wide interval crossing zero; all four blocks adverse; no demonstrated solution. Withdrawn, not combined into selected state.

attributionLimits: Selected boundary complete comparison vs production: spec -4.0280% CI[-5.6391,-2.3894]. Independent comparison vs prior slim prototype: -0.4720% CI[-3.4301,+2.5767]. Do not attribute the complete 4% gain to boundary simplification alone, or transfer old snapshot ratios.
Selected full list guard +29.2559% CI[-2.5553,+71.4520], all four blocks adverse. Previous selected states already showed confirmed list regression; strict non-regression remains unproved.
No new GC/native diagnostic was taken for these exact variants; do not assign old promotion counts or allocation decisions to them.
No repeated eager definition epoch/view-ownership, raw fence bulk-search, physical layout, delimiter arena or disabled-pretenuring acceptance experiment.

line-columns-research-fed4f91-node26-m1p.status: Fully withdrawn: no established primary benefit for the changed storage management. No confirmed regression claimed; no further tuning or secondary timing. Production restored.
line-columns-research-fed4f91-node26-m1p.intent: Test a fixed structure-of-arrays layout for physical and projected lines; reduce stride arithmetic and let the locator walk a contiguous start column without deriving geometry.
model: Replace one interleaved Int32Array with four always-present equal-capacity Int32Array columns: starts, ends, nexts, states.
One BlockLines owner and existing grammar API. No optional states, physical/projected mode, additional getter derivation, sparse locator, lazy fill or row-cursor protocol.
All four facts remain stored per line; physical zero-state writes, relative edit suffix encoding, growth policy, source-order locator and scan reset behavior preserved.

No intermediate facts or active numeric payload eliminated; source representation adds three array wrappers/backing stores per owner and changes copy/growth/slice from one array to four. These are source-level structure facts, not measured total heap or cache costs.
line-columns-research-fed4f91-node26-m1p.historicalDistinction: 68/68b used interleaved coordinate fields with optional state; 29/30/31/42/69 derived or compressed geometry. This candidate keeps four dense fixed columns and direct geometry. Its result does not authorize repeating rejected variants.

orientation.A: previous implementation: unconditional trailing-whitespace trim before title detection
orientation.B: current implementation: trim trailing whitespace inside the present-title branch

explanation.scope: Only the direct inline link/image branch of createBuildMedia. Reference links/images, scanner validation, token schema, AST schema and API signatures unchanged.
changes: Initialize URL to empty string and title to null, eliminating the duplicate empty-resource else branch.
Use the already stored destination boundary to bound initial whitespace skipping. The boundary already existed and was also used by the old implementation.
Skip destination-following whitespace, then trim trailing title whitespace only when content remains.
Plain title-less links avoid the old unconditional backward whitespace test. Title-less links with trailing whitespace still scan that whitespace forward.
explanation.importantQualification: The old implementation already called semanticText for titles only when a title was present. This commit defers trailing-whitespace handling; it does not newly eliminate unconditional title decoding.
explanation.originalTestPolicy: Public createDocument/edit end-to-end test distinguishing absent title null from empty title string; no token-layout/private-field assertions.

list-spread-ownership-node26-m1pro.json.protocol: Node 26.13.0 / Apple M1 Pro; taskpolicy -c utility; alternating ABBA/BAAB; fresh process/module per observation; 250ms warmup/full GC/150ms settling/about 300ms measurement including natural GC; all phases <=500ms. No own build/test/profile overlaps throughput. CPU profiles and work counters separate.

variants.A: Exact Q review build, SHA256 263684f7dd4985a76f85fbebee4a83eb69c34310a5eaf95ce324ac00aad2f7ee; 160358 bytes. Q has known middle-edit regressions versus dcf11a6.
variants.B: Derive listItem.spread in list AST builder from adjacent child positions. Remove generic nested-scan visitor and trailing blank rescans, and ListItemSpreadClose. Ordinary explicit ListItemClose and ListSpreadClose remain. 160238 bytes (-120).
variants.C: Additionally derive list.spread from item positions, remove ListSpreadClose and existing listStart spread state. 159997 bytes (-361). Adds 5221 AST range comparisons on Rust compared with B; spec regression +1.141% established across 12 blocks.
variants.workingMain: Accepted Q+D at 69240f6; 160583 bytes; SHA256 dd573943f5aec969f0295f202a6d254c19f9a11628df078a982e0a29c0717695. No B/C source currently present.

limits: All B/C performance reports compare against Q, not accepted Q+D. No inference of combined gains or non-regression on Q+D. No new remark comparison.

B pooled spec -1.533% and Rust -3.585%; examples/APIs confidence intervals cross zero. Four-block structural/edit guards establish gains in list-blank/list-wide/list-blocks/quote-headings; document/spec and tail remain uncertain.

C was profiled and adjusted back to item-only B. Do not retry unchanged all-list spread derivation. Work counts demonstrate extra comparisons, not exact causal accounting of the small spec regression.

CPU summaries clip sample intervals to the actual measured hrtime window, after individually verifying clock alignment. Inspector startup samples previously inflated totals; uninstrumented ABBA throughput is unaffected. Effective profiler cadence is about 495us despite requested 100us.

Expanded syntax/edit checks find three unique inherited listItem.spread errors corrected by B/C. Other AST fields match baseline; only type/children/spread projection matches the canonical parser. An inherited fenced-code body space mismatch remains, so full canonical AST equality is NOT claimed.

First new normative test incorrectly expected the inherited code body mismatch fixed and failed; corrected test asserts only normative hierarchy/spread. Original failed reports retained. First equal-length diagnostic exercised zero actual equal-length edits and is superseded by expanded coverage (5700 per backend).

B with its two public tests passed 198 tests, typecheck, generated/CSP corpus and edit checks before being set aside for exact-Q review. Current accepted Q+D passes 196 tests and typecheck. No parser-private repository tests added.

literal-content-ownership-dcf11a6-node26.status: Research, not admitted. Q is visible on main with later range-ownership adjustments. All historical batches retained.
literal-content-ownership-dcf11a6-node26.protocol: Node 26.13.0 / M1 Pro, taskpolicy -c utility. Alternating ABBA/BAAB; fresh process/module per observation; 250 ms warmup, full GC, 150 ms settling, approximately 300 ms measured windows including natural GC, each phase capped at 500 ms. CPU/JIT instrumentation is diagnostic only. No simultaneous own build/test/profile during throughput. No M3 validation or new remark ratio. Cross-zero intervals do not prove equivalence.
literal-content-ownership-dcf11a6-node26.model: Literal rules emit final body text, primitive info and exact token spans; scan complete input to convergence instead of expanding artificial EOF windows.
keyFindings: G eager final-text projection regressed repeated fence-window edits (~+13%) and projected fences (~+9.5%). Profiles and work probes identify repeated literal-body construction and per-row concatenation. Do not retry unchanged.

Complete scanning reduces a fence insertion from nine scans / 2324 fence checks to one scan / 802 checks. The old convergence contract remains based on complete record geometry and shifted token equality.

I/M variants passed a starting index through scanBlockLines. Parameter-form changes did not settle adverse results: pooled I APIs +2.09%, pooled M Rust +1.75%, with positive intervals. Do not assert default-parameter scope as cause.
O retains literal ownership improvements but eight-block confirmation showed Rust +1.69% with a positive interval. Rust has zero indented-code calls; indentedContent cannot explain that result.

Q restores the scanBlockLines API, preserving a suffix copy. First four blocks: spec -2.830%, examples -3.867%. Guards: middle insertion +3.417%, middle replacement +7.752%, head -12.614%, fence-window -14.519%. Q alone is not admitted.

For the exact middle replacement, baseline copies 156512 B versus Q 230304 B. Q copies a 4638-row suffix in addition to the writable geometry clone. Slice CPU self samples increase 9.629 -> 11.472 us/edit. This motivates read-only borrowed scan ranges.

Literal Tab semantics improve, but inherited structural indentation / tab closing-fence errors remain. No claim of universal reference equivalence. Failed H/J line-ending variants are archived, not retained.

native-line-kernel-0b724f4-node26-m1pro..status: Rejected execution-backend experiment; no production source changed. SIMD full spec comparison improves, but examples regress substantially, so no admission, cumulative update, thresholds or rescue variants.
native-line-kernel-0b724f4-node26-m1pro..historyDistinction: New execution substrate: UTF16 source encoded directly into Wasm memory, whole physical table produced per call, copied into existing BlockLines. No parser, grammar, token, locator, AST or edit model changes. Unlike native RegExp/split/JS character loops, the second kernel scans 16 bytes per vector step and avoids per-row JS/native String#indexOf calls.
model: Original four-field physical index and range grammar remain canonical. Wasm output is temporary and synchronously copied into the existing index.

Scalar native kernel: 327 bytes. SIMD UTF8 kernel: 428 bytes. UTF16 offset tracking treats 4-byte UTF8 scalars as two code units and TextEncoder replacement of a lone surrogate as one; original source content remains untouched.
JS wrapper adds an encoded input representation, a scratch index representation, typed-array views and a result wrapper. Module initialization failure retains the original JS scanner.
No minify, feature API or codegen removal. Node-specific scratch binary loader and hand-built binary emitter are research artifacts, not production packaging.
productLimits: No browser packaging or deployment claim.
Large-input bounds and memory growth failure behavior were not qualified; output reserves a source-length upper bound rather than the old adaptive retained capacity.
Do not adopt this backend solely from spec result. No source-size thresholds or profile options were added to hide the example regression.

newline-class-and-fence-run-a73acfe-node.status: Measured, not integrated. Not a remark ratio. Production source unchanged.
newline-class-and-fence-run-a73acfe-node.profile: CPU.c0a53f8.cpuprofile summed across nodes: locationAt 135/3162 = 4.3% self. An earlier note cited 1.1% from a single node.

locationAt.attribution: The monotonic cursor crosses the spec line table once. Samples are the call and the object each node must own. A same-line end that still allocates does not remove that object.

newlineClass.question: Can the boundary lookaround be deleted by treating every LF as a class member, leaving the existing newline branch to drop insignificant breaks?
newlineClass.equivalence: On all 814 spec views the non-newline stops match, and the simplified newline-token decisions match. The widened class stops 1167 extra times.
newlineClass.attribution: The extra stops cost more than the lookaround. The existing branch already ignores an insignificant LF, but entering it 1167 times is slower than letting the RegExp skip those newlines.

fenceRuns.attribution: Openers and closers are mostly 32-character marker runs. A tight scalar loop is faster than RegExp complement search and faster than startsWith of an 8-character needle. Unrolling by 4 saves about 0.002 ms, under the harness interval. Deleting the loop entirely is the only way past that interval, and the run length is the fence rule.

newline-class-and-fence-run-a73acfe-node.repeatGate: Do not replace the boundary lookaround with a newline-inclusive class unless a new profile shows those extra stops are cheaper than the lookaround. Do not replace the fence marker-run loop with RegExp.test, startsWith chunks, or a 4-wide unroll unless the run length stops dominating fenceAt and closesFence. Do not add a per-line charCodeAt to #scan to avoid closesFence's 3730 first-char rejects. Do not reopen locationAt sharing or a same-line shortcut that still allocates: the walk is already one forward pass.

next-boundary-research-fed4f91-node26-m1.status: Both candidates completely withdrawn. Consumer-only spec regression is established in the measured four-block batch. Full compact candidate has no established benefit; intervals include zero. No source/test change retained or cumulative update.
next-boundary-research-fed4f91-node26-m1.focusedIntent: Distinguish structural consumption bounds from semantic content ends, then eliminate the redundant stored content-end coordinate without changing grammar dispatch, AST/token ownership, feature API or incremental correspondence.

model.consumerOnly: Whitespace/indent scans, blank detection, paragraph continuation and fence trailing-whitespace checks use next as upper bound and explicitly recognize CR/LF. Partial-range bounds remain enforced; this is not an unbounded source scan. Original four-field storage retained for independent attribution.
model.compact: Store Start, Next and State in three packed slots. Ending width 0/1/2 occupies two explicitly named State bits, lazy uses bit 2 and prefix columns begin at bit 3. End is Next minus width. No source reference, separate class, optional state, sparse index, per-row object, getter cache, new metadata or feature descriptor.
model.historicalDistinction: Unlike 69, which retained End and derived Next, this candidate keeps Next directly. Unlike old compressed getters/row cursors, consumers first reduce End queries. This change in consumption justified one new experiment; it did not justify retuning the failed representations.
model.representationScope: For spec 9756 physical rows, active packed fields 39024 -> 29268; numeric payload 156096B -> 117072B. This is line-index payload only, not total heap reduction or measured cache/GC cost.

diagnostics.scope: Untimed, instrumented bundles never used for timing. Counts are public-method execution counts across physical/projected views, not memory or elapsed attribution.
diagnostics.finding: Spec End calls 12978 -> 4013 (-69.08%); Next calls rise 3506 -> 12471 by the identical 8965 count. This proves query substitution, not fewer total geometry calls. Only the compact candidate eliminates stored coordinates.

paragraph-letter-skip-ab933fb-node26-m1p.question: On a paragraph continuation, if the first code unit is not a space or a tab, can the fallback skip trimLineWhitespaceStart and indentOffset?
paragraph-letter-skip-ab933fb-node26-m1p.shape: One branch in the existing paragraph fallback. A space or a tab still calls both helpers, and a whitespace-only line still breaks before indentOffset. Setext and startsInterruptingBlock stay on every nonblank line. This is not the fused character walk and not the continuation bitmap.
paragraph-letter-skip-ab933fb-node26-m1p.behavior: Spec, rust, public APIs, 652 CommonMark examples, and the same examples with the optional features produced identical JSON, including positions. Edges matched for blank lines, four-space continuations, tabs, block quotes, lists, setext, fences, CR, and CRLF.

freshProcessMediansMs.note: Six alternating fresh processes, 250 ms warmup, one GC, ~280 ms of spec parses, taskpolicy -c utility. Not an ABBA result.

paragraph-letter-skip-ab933fb-node26-m1p.attribution: trimLineWhitespaceStart is 1.35% of position ticks on the head spec profile and indentOffset is 0.22%. On a letter the trim loop already stops at the first character, which is the same load the new branch performs. Whitespace lines still call both helpers. The 400 ms profiles are too coarse to move those frames (about 200 position ticks) and the parse counts are 387 against 388. A −0.22% median gap sits inside the harness noise, whose spec half-width is about 1 percentage point. The earlier fused walk made the fallback slower. The earlier bitmap also skipped setext and startsInterruptingBlock; this branch does not, and that bitmap stays reverted.
paragraph-letter-skip-ab933fb-node26-m1p.repeatGate: Do not add a paragraph-fallback branch whose only job is to skip trimLineWhitespaceStart and indentOffset when the first code unit is not a space or a tab. Resume only if a profile of this bundle shows those two helpers together above about 2% of spec samples and the ticks sit in the multi-character loops, not on the first-character reject. paragraph-prefix-a73acfe-node26-m1pro.js.attribution: On a continuation line the old path calls trimLineWhitespaceStart and then indentOffset, which repeats up to three spaces. The fused loop keeps indentOffset's three-column rule and calls trim only when a tab or a deeper run remains. indentOffset left the profile and trim fell from 0.97% to 0.52%, but the paragraph fallback rose from 1.26% to 2.38%. The character walk is slower inside that larger function than it was in the two helpers. Spec versus the kept absolute bundle is entirely above zero (+0.81% [+0.08, +1.54]). paragraph-prefix-a73acfe-node26-m1pro.js.repeatGate: Do not fuse indentOffset and trimLineWhitespaceStart into the paragraph continuation loop. A tab or a run past three spaces still needs the full trim.

semantic-build-profile-032e0b3-node26-m1.status: Kept as focused model simplification, not an established performance optimization. No cumulative remark ratio update. Table stress timing remains uncertain; no equivalence/universal non-regression claim.
semantic-build-profile-032e0b3-node26-m1.title: refactor: unify block AST traversal through registered builders
semantic-build-profile-032e0b3-node26-m1.intent: Separate structural token indexing from semantic AST selection. Profile builder membership owns semantic selection; eliminate duplicate role classification and feature-specific child walkers.
model: BlockRole no longer distinguishes BlockOpen from FrameOpen. All semantic/nested openers use Open. Close and Leaf values are unchanged; the unused projection Mask is removed.
Register existing list-item/task-item, table-row/cell and component-label builders through the existing profile table. No new feature API or builder signature introduced.
Core buildBlockChildren invokes registered builders and skips unregistered metadata. Remove list item traversal, table row/cell traversal and component label build-then-unshift.
Builder result default widens from RootContent to Node because nested MDAST nodes now participate in the same registry; parser public declarations remain byte-identical.

No token count, token fields, syntax metadata, block lookahead, incremental correspondence, AST ownership or cross-parse cache added. Scanning still indexes ranges and uses the original explicit close protocol.
Internal kind changes only relocate former FrameOpen kinds into the ordinary Open range; no numerical packing, minify gain or unrelated close/leaf renumbering.
semantic-build-profile-032e0b3-node26-m1.retentionReason: Clearer grammar-neutral projection ownership; one fewer role classification and fewer imperative traversals, with no new mutable state or API. Qualified comparisons do not resolve a throughput gain or regression; no speed threshold imposed and all uncertainty is retained.

protocol.method: Alternating ABBA/BAAB; fresh process and module cache per observation; GC before warmup and settling; natural GC included; all samples retained.

performanceInterpretation: Final stock spec -.34377%, examples +.37247%, Rust -.83524%, API +.65534%, tail -.02602%; all CIs cross zero.

The source of the bimodality is not established by allocation/pretenuring logs; do not assert a specific allocator cause or use this to prove equivalence. Exact individual values remain in rawReports.

findings: Default generated branches 21 -> 9. Generated source characters A/F/G 1390/837/771. Exact per-handler spec call counts remain equal, total 1621 each, with identical AST and positions.

findings: The confirmation establishes I spec regression +1.8113%, CI[+0.5558,+3.0825]. First-round document gain -2.2058% does not persist as a resolved gain in confirmation (-0.2908%, CI[-1.7047,+1.1434]). Do not select the favorable first round.

resolvePairedSyntax optimized code is 5720 B in document/spec for A/H/I. Its 1406 printed instruction lines match after declared address normalization. Spec A/I both produce 5408 B; no instruction-equivalence claim was established for spec.

All three document JIT runs invalidate dependent code after full GC and complete 7-8 optimizations during measurement. This identifies tier activity but does not prove it causes the measured regression.

Spec profiled GC time per parse is A 25.912 us / I 24.149 us; short-profile self-time differences are spread over unchanged functions. Inspector start/stop work is visible in the samples. Neither GC amplification nor the changed helper is established as the causal explanation.

The caller-shape hypothesis is not supported. Do not retain I or infer a spec optimization from a cold helper simplification. The original H regression remains unresolved; no throughput claim for the four-edit working tree.

soft-lf-boundary-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.js.question: Can nextBoundaryOffset stop treating a landed line feed as a boundary, leaving soft breaks in the literal gap?
soft-lf-boundary-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.js.behavior: Deleting the charCodeAt === LF return made spec, rust, public APIs, and 652 CommonMark examples produce identical JSON trees, including positions. Hard breaks, CR, and CRLF edges matched too. The slow pattern still matches a whitespace-adjacent break. The deletion is behavior-preserving and is not a speedup.

freshProcessMediansMs.note: Eight alternating fresh processes, 250 ms warmup, one GC, ~280 ms of spec parses, taskpolicy -c utility. Not an ABBA result.

abbaVsHead.specOutlier: Block 5 ABBA opened with head at 1.3042 ms against a neighbor band of 0.87–0.92 ms. That single head sample is the -15.99% block. The other seven spec blocks are -0.96, +0.69, -0.80, +0.81, -0.67, +0.02, -1.66.

soft-lf-boundary-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.js.attribution: The removed statement is the line-feed charCodeAt before RegExp.test. On the head spec profile that call is a small slice of nextBoundaryOffset, which itself is about 2.7%. After the deletion, a 400 ms spec profile still puts the helper at 2.86% (14 self hits of the filtered node set) and those ticks sit on boundary.test at dist line 1341. The boundary class and #scan are unchanged. Isolated 8-block ABBA versus head-base 3b2a9b2b does not establish a spec speedup: -2.47% [-7.31, +2.62]. The width is one head observation at 1.3042 ms, not a faster candidate band. The other seven spec blocks change sign and stay inside about 1.7%. Examples and rust are entirely faster; apis and tail cross zero. No case is entirely slower. Fresh-process medians near -1.8% are the signal that did not survive the paired harness.
soft-lf-boundary-ab933fb-node26-m1pro.js.repeatGate: Do not delete the landed line-feed return in nextBoundaryOffset, and do not split a second fast helper or a per-step ternary around it. Resume only when an 8-block ABBA against this bundle shows the spec interval entirely below zero without a single multi-millisecond outlier carrying the mean. Identical mdast is not evidence of a speedup.

acceptedCandidate.title: perf: stop searching exhausted line-ending streams
acceptedCandidate.mechanism: When lineFeed is -1, the remaining immutable source has already been proved LF-free. Do not run indexOf(LF,next) again after every later CR. Both live cursors continue advancing when applicable. No new state/API/metadata/token format; branch is only reached in CR processing.
acceptedCandidate.algorithmicScope: For CR-only input, repeated LF searches scan successively shorter suffixes, giving quadratic search volume at fixed average line length. Candidate keeps one initial LF search and progressing CR discovery. Does not change parser-wide complexity for arbitrary Markdown.
acceptedCandidate.primary: LF spec +0.7037%, CI[-0.8504%,+2.2821%]; no statistically established benefit or regression, not proof of equivalence.
acceptedCandidate.retentionReason: One added condition eliminates redundant failed searches and produces large CR-only gains; all stock/append-delete intervals cross zero. This is retained as a CR-path algorithmic improvement, not primary-goal progress.

stream-boundary-research-89ce055-node26-.status: Research progress only; no production change or speedup claim. Checkpoint ownership centralized and grammar coverage expanded. Normative reference gate has nine failures; full grammar, semantic/raw bounds and incremental lifecycle still unproven. 100x goal remains active/unmet.
stream-boundary-research-89ce055-node26-.previousGoalTurnClassification: progress: two hypotheses rejected with strict short ABBA; raw-locator regression established that full source rescanning cannot be assumed cheap; restricted semantic-anchor proof established the next ownership problem.
stream-boundary-research-89ce055-node26-.thisTurnClassification: progress: concrete centralized-output implementation, generated start-fact transfer, streamed quote/HTML/indented code/reference prototypes, expanded public AST checks, and new negative evidence changing next model work.
structuralChanges: Feature handlers no longer receive or call locator/checkpoint methods; source-coordinate facts are collected in token output and core scope/EOF lifecycle.

Current-row-only quote cursors consume raw rows through their parent; no physical/projected full line tables. Lazy requests originate from active paragraph scanning, not reverse reconstruction of last line.
Paragraph passes a parsed next-start event directly to core in the same logical scope; no cross-edit/source cache.
Both start and interrupt dispatch are generated once per parser, with CSP fallback using identical feature probes. Non-interrupting definition/indented-code rules are omitted from interrupt dispatch.

Reference lookahead forks/adopts raw/quote cursor-owned scalar state without a whole lookahead row array. Immutable matcher fields may be shared; no arbitrary feature-state deep copy. This parser state model is still provisional.

referenceGate.scope: 8316 explicit-marker/title-fallback inputs pass baseline AST/positions in each backend. Nine separate lazy-definition reference checks fail in each backend. Failures preserved; no claim of completed definition semantics.
referenceGate.reason: A semantic definition AST node cannot simply be modeled as a standalone non-lazy grammar leaf. Prospective paragraph ownership and definition refinement need redesign, not an extra syntax-specific lazy flag.

geometryComparison.sourceDescription: Six quote prefixes, fence with 4000 body rows, no final newline

semanticBoundaryGap.sourceDescription: 4000 indented content rows, 100 trailing blank rows, outside paragraph
semanticBoundaryGap.explanation: Indented code position end is still carried as metadata.contentLength while token span consumes trailing blanks. Emission-time checkpoints do not capture that earlier semantic end; current locator must walk the body again. Requires a uniform semantic/raw-boundary solution, not a syntax-specific checkpoint hook.

openModelRequirements: Separate semantic node completion from prospective paragraph/group lifetime while retaining one BlockRecord per AST root. DependencyEnd must not be finalized before the governing lookahead/group is resolved.

Unify semantic span with consumed raw coverage; current indented-code contentLength metadata can hide the last semantic row from emission-time checkpoints. Do not add feature checkpoint hooks to patch it.
List/extensions and createDocument/visitor/window/convergence remain unsupported. No production fallback/re-scan path was added.
Inspect V8 cursor receiver layouts, fork allocations, output-wrapper inlining and whole-path cost once full grammar is available; row/anchor counts do not prove heap or timing savings.

List item cursors project only their current row. An active paragraph requests underindented lazy continuation; list/quote no longer inverse-probe accumulated line arrays to infer the last leaf. Parsed sibling markers stay grammar-owned and can become a generic pending start event.
Direct block blank separation is summarized in the scope scan; original explicit list/item close tokens and AST builders retained. No new token metadata or production API.
Parser-owned raw cursor, token buffer and anchor storage reused, matching production one-shot ownership; AST positions remain independently allocated.

Semantic locator anchor experiment adds known physical row end to physical start/ordinal, avoiding LF searches within a proven row. Corrected cross-source reset of that end fact before final validation. No claim that fewer fields or searches imply faster parse.

Additional list matrix has 10368 inputs per backend: 9528 complete baseline matches, 840 baseline differences. Of these, 792 match the reference after normalizing line endings; 48 mixed-ending cases differ from the reference. Those 48 match both the prototype and reference on canonical LF source. The diagnostic command intentionally exits 1; this is not an overall correctness pass or a request to waive unresolved semantics.

import json,math,statistics

 for i in range(0,len(runs),4):logs.append(sum(math.log(x['ns'])*(1 if x['variant']=='B' else -1)for x in runs[i:i+4])/2)
def cdf(t,df):
 theta=math.atan(t/math.sqrt(df));integral=theta
 for n in range(2,df,2):integral=math.sin(theta)*math.cos(theta)**(n-1)/n+(n-1)*integral/n
 return .5+math.gamma((df+1)/2)/(math.sqrt(math.pi)*math.gamma(df/2))*integral
def critical(df):
 lo,hi=0,10
 for _ in range(60):
  mid=(lo+hi)/2
  if cdf(mid,df)<.975:lo=mid
  else:hi=mid
 return (lo+hi)/2

table-alignment-model-layout-node26-m1pr.title: refactor: retain table alignments as semantic values

history.distinction: Upstream removed only alignment group structure and retained alignment leaf tokens. The surviving local difference removes those leaves and stores semantic AlignType[] in existing metadata.value. This predated the later unified-block experiment and was outside its rollback, not reintroduced by it. Scope explains survival but is not an acceptance argument.
history.withdrawnExperiment: 71057a5 perf: prune redundant block records uniformly; aeedd44 fix: build component labels before slot bodies

protocol.inspection: Build exact snapshots. Append export {BlockScanner,BlockTokenStream,compileProfile,DocumentImpl} only. Read existing private fields through in-process Node Inspector; no production instance fields or class bodies modified. Capture final native DebugPrint and native elements/property predicates. Int32Array zero-length view verified HaveSameMap with original to avoid printing all integers; byteLength read from original.
protocol.mapCaveat: Map addresses are process-local. Compare descriptors/layout, not cross-process identity. log-maps creation records precede constructor slack tracking: BlockTokenStream initially logs 160 bytes / 17 in-object slots, but final warmed DebugPrint shows 96 bytes / 9 slots on both sides. Final actual sizes come from DebugPrint. HOLEY_ELEMENTS on ordinary objects does not mean dictionary named properties.
protocol.reproduce: taskpolicy -c utility NODE26 FLAGS layout-driver.mjs VARIANT CASE > VARIANT-CASE.debug.log 2>&1; variants before/after/current; cases small4/wide30/two-tall2. No forced GC or ABBA timings; these instrumented processes are layout diagnostics only.

fixtures.small4: 4 columns, header + 1 body row; alignment null/left/center/right.
fixtures.wide30: 30 columns, header + 1 body row; same four alignments cycle.
fixtures.two-tall2: Two 2-column tables, each header + 300 body rows, separated by a blank line. Pure tables: no other feature metadata.

findings.semanticImprovement: Alignment is a table-owned semantic attribute rather than a structural child. Removes encode-to-four-token-kinds then decode-to-AlignType[] loop; table child stream contains only rows. Existing metadata API reused; no new feature/core API or close protocol.
findings.actualLayout: AST table remains 56-byte fast-property object with four in-object fields type/align/children/position. Align remains 32-byte PACKED_ELEMENTS JSArray with identical backing capacities. TokenStream remains 96-byte fast-property object with nine in-object fields. Existing #metadata slot changes from undefined to a newly allocated array for plain tables. One 32-byte fast-property {value} wrapper is added per table; payload array is identical to AST align, not an extra align copy.
findings.smallTableStorage: Records 26 -> 22, used record bytes 416 -> 352, retained Int32 capacity remains 512 bytes. New metadata JSArray is 32 bytes, its observed FixedArray has 17 slots, wrapper 32 bytes. This is added heap structure; fewer used token bytes did not reduce the allocated typed buffer here.
findings.wideTableStorage: Records 156 -> 126; Int32 capacity 4096 -> 2048 bytes because a growth boundary is crossed. Metadata overhead still added. Not a whole-process or whole-heap retained-size measurement.
findings.sparseMetadataStorage: Two long tables: records 3620 -> 3616; retained Int32 buffer stays 65536 bytes. New metadata length 1809 with only indices 0 and 1808; actual Map is DICTIONARY_ELEMENTS backed by NumberDictionary[16]. Named properties remain fast. Existing sparse metadata infrastructure, newly exercised by otherwise plain tables; not proof of deoptimization or throughput regression.
findings.ownership: Before rebuild created a fresh alignment array. After/current retained table tokens can give old/new AST table nodes the same align array when a distant definition change rebuilds inline content. Document.tree is document-owned and callers must not morph it, so sharing is compatible with the current public contract; it adds cross-stage read-only ownership reliance.
findings.invalidation: Equal-width :--- -> ---: changes alignment left -> right. Before narrowed token interval is [7,8) -> [7,8); after/current [14,14) -> [14,14), i.e. empty. Object payload values are not deep-compared, and TableOpen has a zero-width span. Correctness comes from block source damage causing root rebuild plus full replacement metadata copying, independently of narrowed token damage. No correctness bug observed; token equality is not semantic payload equality.
findings.scope: c50e71a still creates temporary numeric delimiter cell ranges before semantic alignments. Their elimination belongs to later 2037f4d, not this commit. Later 766d9f9 changes cell-range derivation. Current layout matches exact after for these fixtures but is not used for causal throughput attribution.
findings.judgment: The semantic direction and feature-local control flow are clearer, but the current integration is not an unconditional overall model simplification: it exchanges dense structural entries for sparse heap metadata and relies on shared ownership and two distinct change boundaries. Token count alone is insufficient acceptance evidence. No new performance benefit is claimed and no new protocol should be added merely to justify this candidate.

scope: All structural frame completions use one End scan event. End events do not persist in the flat stream; no close(value) API or metadata payload extension.

List spread is a kind flag. Ordered-list start numbers and normalized component names are retained semantic facts rather than reread headers.

Inline correspondence matches mapped source anchors, then existing text/definition dependency checks decide token reuse. Root retention still requires whole-block convergence; oldRecordEnd fix retained. Dead oldRecordStart scan removed.
